name: Girls Against Boys
label: Touch and Go
lede: A Fugazi drummer's side project that grew two bass players, moved to New York, made three sleek, sleazy records for Touch and Go, then walked into Geffen just as Geffen stopped existing.

eras.title: A Fugazi side project called Skind
eras.text: Girls Against Boys started as studio tinkering by Eli Janney and Fugazi drummer Brendan Canty, a way out of the post-hardcore both were known for. When Soulside ended, its singer-guitarist and rhythm section drifted in, and the side project became a band.

years.h: Eli Janney and Brendan Canty's duo, Skind, adds Scott McCloud
years.p: Eli Janney and [[Brendan Canty|8b505ef0-c5a7-4deb-bc32-27c882f3c40e]] start a studio project called Skind, then recruit [[Soulside|de2e8176-32c2-4abe-b718-9392dffd8ffe]] guitarist Scott McCloud to sing. A 1989 session produces three industrial-disco tracks.
years.xp: The name Girls Against Boys, per Wikipedia, was a nod to ordinary gender rivalries. Canty was also the drummer in [[Fugazi|233fc3f3-6de2-465c-985e-e721dbabbace]], and the project began as a place for him and Janney to try music that wasn't post-hardcore.

years.h: Soulside ends; Johnny Temple and Alexis Fleisig join GVSB
years.p: After Bobby Sullivan breaks up [[Soulside|de2e8176-32c2-4abe-b718-9392dffd8ffe]], bassist Johnny Temple and drummer Alexis Fleisig try a short-lived band, Little Baby, with [[Mike Fellows|58a7226f-e06a-4728-82a5-ddc4443025a4]], then commit to Girls Against Boys. Brendan Canty leaves to focus on [[Fugazi|233fc3f3-6de2-465c-985e-e721dbabbace]].

years.h: Nineties vs. Eighties: the 1989 and 1990 bands, back to back
years.p: Girls Against Boys' debut EP puts the 1989 disco session on an "Eighties" side and the harder early-1990 session on a "Nineties" side. It first came out on Eli Janney's novelty label, Slate Records.

years.h: Guitarist Luke Wood passes through, headed for the music business
years.p: Luke Wood plays guitar in Girls Against Boys briefly, then leaves during the first album sessions for a label career and his band Sammy. Seven years later he signs GVSB to Geffen.

eras.title: Two basses in New York
eras.text: McCloud, Temple and Fleisig talked Janney into leaving Florida for New York, and the band's odd engine locked in: Temple on bass, Janney on a second bass plus keyboards and samples. Touch and Go and producer Ted Niceley turned that into Venus Luxure No. 1 Baby.

years.h: First big U.S. tour, opening for Fugazi
years.p: Girls Against Boys, now based in New York with Eli Janney back from Florida, spend early 1992 opening for [[Fugazi|233fc3f3-6de2-465c-985e-e721dbabbace]] across the U.S.

years.h: Tropic of Scorpio, self-produced by Eli Janney
years.p: Girls Against Boys' first album comes out on Adult Swim Records, with guests including [[Nathan Larson|c0845dd8-ef14-486c-92b6-260727732b4c]] of [[Shudder to Think|5a6e19e0-3ff0-4b3d-869e-3c539d6d8707]] and parts from departed guitarist Luke Wood.

years.cap: Venus Luxure No. 1 Baby, Touch and Go, 1993
years.h: Venus Luxure No. 1 Baby: GVSB's Touch and Go debut
years.p: Produced by Ted Niceley, whom Eli Janney had assisted in the studio in the 1980s, Venus Luxure No. 1 Baby later landed in 1001 Albums You Must Hear Before You Die.
years.xp:
Scott McCloud named his main cues as avant-garde English punk like [[Joy Division|9a58fda3-f4ed-4080-a3a5-f457aac9fcdd]], plus [[Big Black|9463868f-edc8-427e-ac07-ea89698e5f15]], [[Einstürzende Neubauten|6e9ac29b-798c-4af7-8d9e-55cdc72a999c]], [[Skinny Puppy|5a24bc1a-c093-4a82-84ed-8d7f2da0570d]], [[Sonic Youth|5cbef01b-cc35-4f52-af7b-d0df0c4f61b9]] and [[Killing Joke|f5aca88c-e3c1-4bc2-af33-68a9a9f7b56a]]. He said his words come from late-night bar talk: phrases overheard, repeated until they sound like slogans.

In 2006 the band played the whole album start to finish at All Tomorrow's Parties in London.

years.h: Lollapalooza side stage, then tours with the Jesus Lizard and Helmet
years.p: Girls Against Boys play the side stage of the 1993 Lollapalooza tour, then go out with [[The Jesus Lizard|dfebd6c0-dae7-4cc8-a8e9-0dbaa382209f]], [[Helmet|582fee78-d934-4603-9f5c-1729e0ca36b7]] and [[Jawbox|016fba14-1fc6-4986-86c2-2113ec9b28de]].

eras.title: Sex rock on an indie budget
eras.text: Three Touch and Go albums in three years made GVSB the label's closest thing to rock stars: slick suits, a Clerks song, late-night TV, UK chart entries and a Spin top-five album. It was the peak of their run.

years.h: "Sexy Sam" single, and a song in Kevin Smith's Clerks
years.p: Girls Against Boys put out "Sexy Sam" as a stopgap single. "Kill the Sexplayer" lands on the soundtrack to Kevin Smith's Clerks, and the band plays Lollapalooza's side stage again.

years.h: Cruise Yourself, the second Ted Niceley record
years.p: Cruise Yourself reaches No. 9 on the UK Rock & Metal Albums chart, and "(I) Don't Got a Place" scrapes the UK singles chart at No. 91.

years.h: TV debut on The Jon Stewart Show
years.p: Girls Against Boys play "Don't Got a Place" and "Kill the Sexplayer" on The Jon Stewart Show, then return in May for "Raindrop" and "Cruise Your New Baby Fly Self".

years.h: A Joy Division cover, "She's Lost Control", with its own video
years.p: Girls Against Boys cover [[Joy Division|9a58fda3-f4ed-4080-a3a5-f457aac9fcdd]]'s "She's Lost Control" for the tribute album A Means to an End. Released as a single with a video, it reaches No. 98 in the UK.

years.h: House of GVSB: No. 5 on Spin's albums of 1996
years.p: The third Touch and Go album reaches No. 76 on the UK albums chart. Lead single "Super-Fire" gets to No. 82, the band's best UK singles showing, and to No. 36 on the UK dance chart.

years.h: Rage Against the Machine, Reading, and a third Lollapalooza
years.p: Girls Against Boys tour with [[Therapy?|85226286-349a-4046-8dcf-f75b32baa6b1]] and [[Rage Against the Machine|3798b104-01cb-484c-a3b0-56adc6399b80]], play HFStival in Washington and England's Reading Festival, and join Lollapalooza for a third and final summer.

eras.title: The majors come calling, then collapse
eras.text: Every label wanted them, and they made the majors wait until the Touch and Go deal was done. They signed to Geffen through their own ex-guitarist, made their most expensive record, and watched the label vanish in a merger.

years.h: Eli Janney DJs and remixes; GVSB play the first Fuji Rock
years.p: In a quiet year, Eli Janney works as a New York DJ and remixes [[Sneaker Pimps|696d8523-39a0-44e2-9add-afaa183a2f46]]. Girls Against Boys play the inaugural Fuji Rock Festival in Japan, and Spin lists them No. 38 among its most vital artists.

q: It only made the majors go more crazy.
years.h: GVSB sign a three-album Geffen deal through ex-guitarist Luke Wood
years.p: Girls Against Boys finish their three-album Touch and Go commitment first, then sign with Geffen, where former guitarist Luke Wood is now an executive. Recording with producer Nick Launay starts in October 1997.
years.xp: Scott McCloud said the band's loyalty to Touch and Go only made the majors want them more. Labels were putting them up in luxury hotels at the same time the band was playing punk squats in Italy.

years.h: Freak*on*ica: six months in the studio, electronics up front
years.p: Girls Against Boys' Geffen debut took nearly six months, against the one or two a Touch and Go record got. It reaches No. 11 on Billboard's Heatseekers chart; "Park Avenue" reaches No. 28 on Mainstream Rock.

years.h: On-screen in 200 Cigarettes, and a song in the Psycho remake
years.p: Girls Against Boys appear in the film 200 Cigarettes and cover "Boogie Wonderland" for its soundtrack. "Psycho-Future" goes on the Psycho remake soundtrack, and the band plays Late Night with Conan O'Brien.

q: There's a tension within the personalities of the group.
years.h: Touring with Garbage, GVSB learn Geffen is being shut down
years.p: Freak*on*ica is GVSB's best seller yet but misses Geffen's targets. Then Seagram buys the label's parent, and Scott McCloud is told mid-tour with [[Garbage|f9ef7a22-4262-4596-a2a8-1d19345b8e50]] that Geffen will cease to exist on January 1, 1999.
years.xp:
In the Universal restructuring that followed, the band was moved to Interscope, then parted ways over what Wikipedia calls various conflicts. For almost two years Girls Against Boys could barely record or tour, and demos for a 2000 album stalled.

Looking back in 2013, Scott McCloud said the friction between the four of them was part of the sound, not a problem to solve.

years.h: GVSB score the reality-TV satire Series 7: The Contenders
years.p: Girls Against Boys write the score for the film Series 7: The Contenders. Late in 2001 they sign with the indie label Jade Tree.

years.h: You Can't Fight What You Can't See on Jade Tree
years.p: Back with Ted Niceley, Girls Against Boys headline a tour with the [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs|584c04d2-4acc-491b-8a0a-e63133f4bfc4]] opening. After Australian dates Eli Janney leaves for a family emergency, and [[Sohrab Habibion|6e133bae-8f26-4f44-b1a1-622e051630be]] of Edsel fills in across Europe.
play: You Can't Fight What You Can't See

eras.title: A band in bits and pieces
eras.text: No label, no new album, but GVSB never quite stopped: a stint as an actress's backing band, anniversary shows, short European runs every February. Then in 2009 everything went silent for four years.

years.h: GVSB become Gina Gershon's backing band
years.p: Without Eli Janney, Girls Against Boys back actress Gina Gershon on a tour for her film Prey for Rock & Roll, filmed for the series Rocked with Gina Gershon (2004).

years.h: Brainiac's John Schmersal fills in for Eli Janney
years.p: [[John Schmersal|9f0f837b-e427-4611-aef4-5db88298bfaf]] of [[Brainiac|8db9ae5b-4412-434a-aedd-dc2bb316c355]] and [[Enon|ce49b1f2-a903-46fc-8b84-b5699f019a06]] covers for Eli Janney on a short European tour. He will fill the same spot in 2013 and 2026.

years.h: Touch and Go's 25th anniversary block party in Chicago
years.p: Girls Against Boys play Touch and Go's 25th anniversary party. The same year they play Venus Luxure No. 1 Baby in full at All Tomorrow's Parties in London.

years.h: First trip to Russia, then four years of silence
years.p: Girls Against Boys play Russia for the first time in February 2009. From then until early 2013 there are no shows, releases or updates.

eras.title: The long tail of the House
eras.text: An email between McCloud and Janney about writing songs turned into a reunion, a new EP and a slow, unhurried second life. Meanwhile the members built other careers: a late-night TV bandleader, a publisher, a punk supergroup.

years.h: "It's a Diamond Life": the first GVSB song in 11 years
years.p: Girls Against Boys announce their reunion with a new song. Scott McCloud told Stereogum it began when he and Eli Janney emailed about writing together and decided it should be a GVSB song.

years.h: The Ghost List EP, self-released via Epitonic
years.p: Girls Against Boys' first new release since 2002 comes out online. That month they play the Black Cat's anniversary show in Washington, with John Schmersal again filling in for Eli Janney.

years.h: Eli Janney becomes music director on Late Night with Seth Meyers
years.p: Eli Janney plays keyboards and serves as musical director for the 8G Band on Late Night with Seth Meyers. Johnny Temple, meanwhile, runs Akashic Books, the Brooklyn publisher he founded in 1997.

years.h: Scott McCloud's 50th birthday show, and a Brainiac film party
years.p: Girls Against Boys play just twice in 2017: a Prague show at Lucerna Music Bar for Scott McCloud's 50th birthday, and a release party for a [[Brainiac|8db9ae5b-4412-434a-aedd-dc2bb316c355]] documentary.

years.h: Johnny Temple forms Fake Names with Brian Baker and Dennis Lyxzén
years.p: Johnny Temple starts [[Fake Names|a4271e33-8969-4dd8-9e3c-88b269e89fe0]] with [[Brian Baker|1fd36abf-e43c-4b01-820b-d7280cc27ea5]], [[Michael Hampton|4ed83c42-6348-4368-903e-9116bfa49b8e]] and [[Dennis Lyxzén|d7bb37a5-3d48-4a2f-a761-fe66d5cdb409]]; their debut is on Epitaph. Brendan Canty drums on the 2021 EP.

years.cap: House of GVSB, reissued by Touch and Go in 2022
years.h: Touch and Go reissues House of GVSB with a disc of extras
years.p: Announced in August 2021, the House of GVSB reissue adds a full tracklist of B-sides and outtakes. Girls Against Boys tour the U.S. and Europe behind it through 2022.

years.h: Back in Japan with Soulside, for the first time since 1997
years.p: Girls Against Boys tour Japan with [[Soulside|de2e8176-32c2-4abe-b718-9392dffd8ffe]], Scott McCloud's first band. It's GVSB's first Japan trip since 1997 and Soulside's first ever.

years.h: Australian tour for the Cruise Yourself reissue
years.p: Girls Against Boys return to Australia to mark the remastered Cruise Yourself on vinyl, with John Schmersal standing in for Eli Janney.

sources.title: Washington Post: Getting Together With Girls Against Boys (1996)
